queued_update_semantics: Poll passes immutable source/anchor timestamps with face/hint; it never substitutes UI refresh time as a source timestamp.

Use one pending latest display record and at most one GTK delivery callback; a newer pending record replaces the older one. Keep this queue independent of existing settings-save pending/condition fields.

On GTK delivery, check existing visibility gate and the original250/500ms rule again. Expired/invalid/future timestamps yield face=None/uncertain label and hide all five blue windows. Geometry/threshold classification/control code stays unchanged.
timer_semantics: All display generation/deadline/timer bookkeeping is owned by the GTK thread; poll only publishes the pending record.
For a valid rendered record, schedule timeout for max(1,deadline_ms-now_ms). A timeout is a wakeup, not additional source validity. Recheck now/deadline at callback entry.
If generation tokens are used, a timer tagged with an older generation returns False before hiding any current box OR clearing the handle of a newer timer.

Equivalent one-timer implementation may read the current display deadline when it fires: if a newer valid record extended it, rearm to that current deadline; never hide using the previous record deadline.
At actual expiry hide only the five blue face windows and set uncertain display text; do not hide/move boundary lines or call pan_stop/set_ratio/save/reset/any motor command.

On hide/page exit/close, invalidate display generation, clear deadline and latest pending face, remove its tracked timer on GTK if present and make stale delivery/timer callbacks no-ops. Check closed/active before re-showing or touching destroyed windows.
